summary: Jim and Niels discuss April 2024: trend-following update, option positioning and deleveraging, and the 2024 outlook. Jim argues path and flows matter more than news or direction: market structure and Fed/Treasury liquidity favour upside with squeezes, while rates and a politicized Fed are longer-term risks. Calls for long-dated calls with short stock, hedging a late-May to June tail, and relative bets on Europe/China.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: we just had GDP come out um again weaker now than expected and uh and then we have a hot C you know hot CPI at the same time
claims.claim: Weak GDP together with hot CPI marks a stagflationary environment that markets have not yet priced.
claims.indicator: GDP surprise vs expectations; CPI surprise
claims.testable: partly: surprise series exist but pricing-in is judged by the speaker

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we thought that interest rates would go higher and they'll over the next few years will continue to move higher at some stage
claims.claim: Interest rates are expected to keep moving higher over the next few years.
claims.testable: no: a broad forecast without a defined signal

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the China 10-year government bond yield decreased to an all-time low of 2.22%
claims.claim: A record-low Chinese 10-year yield signals a weaker Chinese economy than it appears.
claims.conditions: may not be a freely traded yield
claims.testable: partly: yield is observable, inference to growth is loose

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: how flat skew has gotten in the vault complex started out very low and into the most recent decline has gotten even lower
claims.claim: Equity-option skew is near historic lows and stayed low even through a decline, which is unusual and a topic of focus for volatility traders.
claims.testable: yes: skew is observable and can be compared with history

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: coffee cocoa both up about 16% for the month that's going to be helping Trend followers
claims.claim: April trend-follower gains came from soft commodities (coffee, cocoa up about 16%), copper at a 2-year high and a record-weak yen, while bonds fell and equities lagged.
claims.direction: long soft commodities, long copper, short yen
claims.conditions: trend followers with slower models stayed short bonds
claims.testable: yes: monthly market returns are observable

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the Yen uh that has been a good source of returns with an incredibly weak uh level this morning hitting a 34-year low
claims.claim: The yen hit a 34-year low with the BoJ holding rates, and the trend may have further to run.
claims.conditions: while BoJ holds rates
claims.testable: partly: a specific market view with a loose end

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer finished at 52 last night so that's confirming the good environment for Trend followers
claims.claim: A trend barometer reading of 52 confirms a good environment for trend followers.
claims.testable: partly: barometer definition not given here

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: sck genen CTA up 1.5% for the month up 11.3% for the year
claims.claim: CTA industry indices were up about 1.4-1.5% in April and 11-13% year to date, with the short-term traders index the best.
claims.indicator: BarclayHedge/SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-term Traders indices

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the MSI World index was down 3.8% in April but still up 4.34% for the year world government bonds down almost 2% in April
claims.claim: In April MSCI World fell 3.8% and the S&P 500 total return fell 3.85% while world government bonds fell almost 2%, so trend followers had little help from stocks and bonds that month.
claims.indicator: MSCI World; world government bond index; S&P 500 TR

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the more people pile into it right and the more people pile pile into it then it eventually reflexively right has um you know some some feedback loops that that then prevent the trend in the short term
claims.claim: Positioning is correlated with trend: the more a trend works, the more people pile in, which creates feedback loops that cause short-term pullbacks without necessarily ending the trend.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: call speculation has been uh you know fairly rampant uh until a little more recently
claims.claim: Call speculation was rampant after the November-March equity trend, which is the typical behaviour of a strong positive trend.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: that type of positioning um tends to uh exacerbate the move right it tends to push leverage into move
claims.claim: Call speculation first exacerbates a rally because it pushes leverage and gamma into the move.
claims.conditions: early stage of the move
claims.testable: partly: gamma estimates exist but are model-based

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: those vix calls uh can can start to uh increase Vol on the on the way up and really unpin um volatility broadly
claims.claim: Buying VIX calls lifts volatility on the way up and unpins volatility broadly, which can create downside volatility eventually (blowoff-top dynamic).
claims.indicator: VIX call buying, vol of vol
claims.conditions: late stage rallies
claims.testable: partly: VIX call activity is observable, effect is stated qualitatively

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: late stages of rallies when I say late stages I mean the last year or two of a big kind of trend rally this is what we tend to see
claims.claim: In the last year or two of a big rally, market-up/vol-up dynamics appear (1998-2000, 2007); the last moves are bigger because of squeezes, and things get frothy.
claims.direction: bigger final upside squeezes, more vol
claims.conditions: last 1-2 years of a trend rally; does not mean the end is months away
claims.testable: partly: spot-vol correlation measurable, identifying late stage is not

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: I would I would expect uh that that these uh this this speculative action will continue to increase volid of the route and create more volatility into the coming um rally
claims.claim: Continuing call speculation should raise vol of vol and volatility during the coming rally.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the more concentrated and leverage positioning is short in the VA Market the more risk there is for markets and we've seen this again and again and again
claims.claim: Concentrated, leveraged positioning in the volatility market raises risk of liquidity stress when big players must absorb it.
claims.testable: partly: positioning data is hard to get

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the co crash to a great extent had others uh along with them uh buying you know March uh Opex right corly Opex option you know options that eventually uh created massive gamma leverage into an Opex cycle
claims.claim: Large option buying into a quarterly expiry created massive gamma leverage that contributed to the Covid crash, an example of kindling for a liquidity event.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: all the autoc colable uh you know Snowball uh options have have a you know have a significant effect on on the decline there
claims.claim: China autocallable snowball structured products amplified the decline in Chinese equities; such structures raise odds of steeper structural declines.
claims.testable: no: notional exposure is rarely public

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: if you're looking at speculating over the course of a year or two for this would be the time to start actively managing a long ball portfolio
claims.claim: The speaker thinks we are late in the cycle, so it is time to start actively managing a long-volatility portfolio over the next year or two.
claims.conditions: late-cycle froth

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: I often say it's very hard to predict Direction it's very easy to well not easy but it's easier to predict distribution
claims.claim: It is easier to predict the distribution of outcomes (high versus low probability paths) than direction, and betting on those paths is as profitable.
claims.testable: partly: depends on how probabilities are estimated

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: oh things are good so we're going up or the inflation number is bad so we're going down or there's a war in the Middle East so we're going down
claims.claim: Deterministic news-to-direction thinking is wrong; market moves are driven by supply and demand reaction functions, so apparent randomness hides rational paths.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: we have the ability to bet um you know in time and space right uh and moneyness um in in very specific ways on path
claims.claim: Options let a trader bet on specific paths (time, price and moneyness) instead of two-dimensional direction, which is where the opportunity lies.
claims.testable: partly: path bets can be built, edge unproven

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: if the market continues to rally um they actually uh these some position I can create gamma they can create a positive momentum in the market
claims.claim: Long positioning is both potential energy for a selloff and fuel for squeezes; if the market keeps rising, levered longs add momentum (as in 1997-2000).
claims.conditions: depends on the trigger: unwinds only if a negative event forces selling
claims.testable: partly: positioning is measurable, outcome is path dependent

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: each year there were an average of two declines of greater than 10 %
claims.claim: In 1997-2000 despite strong years, there were on average two declines of more than 10% a year, so heavy long positioning produced volatility in both directions.
claims.conditions: strong rally years with levered longs

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: long long dated calls and short stock that ball to the upside is too cheap the right tail in particular is too cheap
claims.claim: Long-dated calls hedged with short stock are attractive because upside volatility, the right tail, is too cheap, and the hedge also pays on declines.
claims.indicator: long-dated call implied vol vs realised
claims.conditions: when positioning and structural demand imbalance create two-sided vol
claims.testable: yes: implied vs realised can be backtested

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: Fridays are not the same as every other day a circumstance where entities are not willing to buy because there was a long weekend
claims.claim: Geopolitical news on a Friday before a weekend creates sellers but no buyers (weekend risk, illiquidity), which can push prices to triggers that start deleveraging.
claims.conditions: shocks arriving into a weekend or expiry week

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: has very little to do with Market long-term performance
claims.claim: Geopolitical events like Iran-Israel matter for market path through positioning and liquidity, not for long-term market performance.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: if there's any area of the market that you can look at uh to tell you what was happening and tell you was deleveraging you can just look at HED fund names
claims.claim: Hedge fund longs fell sharply while shorts did not, which reveals deleveraging, so hedge fund long/short baskets are a diagnostic for a deleveraging event.
claims.indicator: hedge fund long and short basket performance
claims.testable: yes: prime-broker baskets can be tracked

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: every morning what happened no matter how big that rally it was sold
claims.claim: Morning rallies from vanna/charm flows being sold each day signal ongoing deleveraging, so rallies are likely to be sold until rebalancing finishes.
claims.conditions: during deleveraging after a technical break
claims.testable: partly: pattern is observable, rule not defined

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the market would have continued about its merry way to the upside
claims.claim: Without the Iran attack the market would have kept rising, perhaps hitting a roadblock a month later, showing path matters more than news.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: all the levered entities right at the end of the month now have to take their risk to constant to where it was last month
claims.claim: After a down month, levered entities must rebalance risk at month end and beginning of month, creating negative flow that resists a rally.
claims.direction: selling pressure after a down month
claims.conditions: after a significant drawdown month

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: when that event comes off the table regardless of what the FED says I don't care what the FED says there's stock to be bought
claims.claim: Event volatility before a Fed meeting leaves dealers short stock against event puts; when the event passes the hedge comes off and dealers must buy stock regardless of the news.
claims.indicator: event-dated implied vol / put positioning around Fed meeting
claims.conditions: when event vol is elevated relative to neighbouring expiries

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: these alos and functions are basically saying okay by May 1 fed we need to be back to X risk level and so that deleveraging continues essentially till that point
claims.claim: Algorithmic and risk-target funds need to reach their target risk before the Fed event, so deleveraging continues until that date, then a window opens.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: then you get the positive flows coming from May Opex and all the the the V charm flows we talk about for the next two weeks because we get into that very positive part of the options cycle
claims.claim: Positive vanna and charm flows around monthly option expiry give a positive period in the first half of the options cycle after the Fed/Treasury events.
claims.conditions: post-expiry window; helped by accommodative Treasury refunding (QRA)

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: this is why time is also not linear you have events they're minutes and hours that matter more than minutes and hours and dramatically so
claims.claim: Time is not linear: event windows matter much more than equal-length periods without events, so forecasts should be tied to the event calendar.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: then you don't want to be short you want to be buying the dips again
claims.claim: If, after deleveraging, price recovers above technical levels with positive momentum in the 1-15 May window, buy the dips; if not, risk rises (if-then path rule).
claims.indicator: technical levels, momentum within a time window
claims.conditions: needs momentum within roughly a week or two; otherwise risk of further deleveraging
claims.testable: yes: conditional rule can be coded

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: there is a ton of and more than usual open interest in the June Opex
claims.claim: Large open interest in the June expiry (VIX call speculation, vol buying in the long end, Fed meeting beforehand) makes it a potential trigger for a leveraged unwind.
claims.indicator: open interest at the June quarterly expiry
claims.conditions: a quarterly expiry with structured products and a Fed meeting

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: there's already been a bit of weakness that's been building for several months in the longer end of the curve
claims.claim: Weakness building in the long end of the vol curve (front decays, back bought) shows demand for protection and speculation.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: when you go to five weeks you go from one to one and a half weeks of week you know without positive flows potential risk in the market to two and a half right
claims.claim: A five-week option cycle lengthens the window without vanna/charm support from about 1-1.5 weeks to about 2.5 weeks, raising the chance of a breakdown.
claims.conditions: five-week monthly cycles
claims.testable: yes: testable on 4 vs 5 week cycles

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: it's a quarterly and there's lots of Structured Products
claims.claim: Quarterly expiries are bigger because of structured products, so June is a concentration point for risk.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: so there is a tail sitting out there and the time window is very clear
claims.claim: A tail risk with a clear time window (late May to mid June) exists, so hedge for it with options.
claims.conditions: if weakness persists after 1-15 May

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: provided it doesn't happen the last two weeks uh and the momentum doesn't come down and ball doesn't respond if V's still pinned in that window you better get back on uh you know long in this market
claims.claim: If momentum holds and vol stays pinned through the dangerous window, get back long, since the pullback will be bought and highs retested.
claims.conditions: vol not responding to decline

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: primarily because the fed and the treasury are telling you there's a put on this Market there's only so much that this thing could decline before they react with more stimulus
claims.claim: 2024 should still be a positive year because the Fed and Treasury effectively put a floor under markets and would respond to declines with stimulus.
claims.conditions: election year, policy put
claims.testable: partly: policy put hard to quantify

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: stocks bonds any asset is two-dimensional you can only bet up and down you cannot bet on path
claims.claim: Stocks and bonds only offer direction while options express the full distribution of outcomes, so options are the superior technology for betting on path.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: this is why the sibo stock is at alltime highs this is why their volumes at alltime highs
claims.claim: Options volume and exchange (Cboe) volumes are at record highs, driven by product proliferation, retail access and education.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they are wonderful in the hands of the professional not always in the hands of everyone
claims.claim: Option strategies are powerful for professionals but can hurt non-professionals because they cut both ways.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: upside Trends uh or long Trends are very hard to turn it takes really long time
claims.claim: Upside trends turn slowly, with long tops or parabolic endings.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they seem to turn much quicker uh like we saw in in March of 2020
claims.claim: Downside trends reverse much faster than upside trends, perhaps because central banks step in with a put.
claims.conditions: central bank intervention

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: you don't buy insurance to protect yourself on the on the upside you do it on the downside this is why skew exists
claims.claim: Everyone is structurally long assets and buys downside protection, so skew exists and creates a risk premium on the downside.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: it's better by the way to than being long stock to be short and out of the money put and long and out of the money call
claims.claim: Short OTM puts plus long OTM calls collect the embedded downside risk premium and beat being long stock.
claims.indicator: OTM put vs OTM call implied vol
claims.direction: short OTM puts, long OTM calls

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: 95% of the time that means that buyback flow is there that perpetuates the upcycle
claims.claim: Because the market is net long puts, dealer hedging gives buyback flow about 95% of the days, which perpetuates up cycles; small declines are profitable to hedgers and bought, so a real decline has to be big.
claims.conditions: most days; fails in tail events
claims.testable: partly: dealer position estimates are model-based

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: it's the FED it's treasury it's BuyBacks you know the world is making money markets go up over time
claims.claim: Structural buyers (Fed, Treasury, buybacks) make demand tilted over supply, so equity trends tend to be upward.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the way it works in terms of distribution is fat left tail right distributed
claims.claim: The return distribution has a fat left tail because of bankruptcy, liquidity and gamma risk; triggering downside gamma perpetuates selling.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the overwhelming majority of time is a blowoff top and this is what you and I have talked about and that happens structurally when VA becomes unpinned
claims.claim: Declines usually come as a blowoff top: vol is lifted off the ground, potential energy builds, and the tail is then crossed and liquidation comes all at once.
claims.testable: partly: hard to define blowoff top ex ante

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: remember the market creates its own stimulus right if the market goes up guess what economy does better
claims.claim: Rising markets stimulate the economy through wealth effects (including crypto), so equities can go higher without Fed rate cuts.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: how do they matter they act with a significant lag and they don't affect a lot of entities UPF front right
claims.claim: Higher rates act with a lag and merely sequester liquidity, so they matter medium to long term but little short term; negative effects will come eventually but can take a long time.
claims.conditions: medium to long horizon

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: QT QE different story direct impact on markets
claims.claim: QE/QT and fiscal stimulus have a direct and immediate impact on markets, unlike interest rate changes.
claims.testable: yes: central bank balance sheet and deficit series

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: that hundred billion dollars we just passed again for military aid uh that's not just going to another country by the way that's going to us you know contractors
claims.claim: Fiscal aid passes into domestic contractor income immediately, so it is more direct stimulus than rates.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: liquidity is actually not weak you know liquidity is very stimulative and has been despite interest rates going higher
claims.claim: Liquidity is very stimulative in this window despite higher rates, so short-term flows favour buyers.
claims.conditions: election year, fiscal stimulus

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the average return during the elections election years during that 14-year period was 211%
claims.claim: Even during the 1968-82 period when the market went nowhere, election years had strongly positive average returns because the Fed and Treasury support them.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: China China's not going to move and do something dramatic we talked about this before the election they want to see what happens right
claims.claim: Election uncertainty keeps entities from acting until results are known, with stimulus coming into the election and unknown thereafter.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the fed's uh Cho choosing of growth over inflation is not a coincidence it is political
claims.claim: The Fed's choice of growth over inflation is political and the politicization is structural, likely worse under Trump, resulting in worse inflation and a bigger right tail for markets.
claims.direction: inflation up, equities right tail up

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: it's other two benefits two responsibilities is one two control volatility so make sure where there's no tail in the market smooth the business Cycles
claims.claim: Beyond price stability and employment, the Fed is meant to control volatility and smooth cycles, implicitly putting a floor under markets.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: there are structural incentives and people always and entities always follow in sentence
claims.claim: Powell acts to preserve the Fed's independence, so structural incentives rather than conspiracy explain Fed behaviour.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: I agree with you that is a potential risk but it's an upside risk if you ask me in the short term uh and and a bigger structural uh problem for markets longer term
claims.claim: Loss of Fed independence is an upside risk for markets short term but a bigger structural problem long term.
claims.direction: equities up short term, down long term

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: when things when narrative gets so far and that people are so convinced of impending doom that sometimes we miss some very important things
claims.claim: When bearish narratives on China become extreme and uniform, look for silver linings and contrarian relative opportunities.
claims.conditions: extreme consensus pessimism

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: Trump could be very very good ultimately after some increased volatility um for an actual deal with China happening if Trump gets elected
claims.claim: A Trump presidency may initially hurt China with tariffs but ultimately lead to a US-China deal.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: the energy issues that are tied to a lot of that are being reversed and commodity uh you know you know pricing is coming down partially because lack of lack of growth
claims.claim: European energy problems are reversing as commodity prices decline, giving a reason for European rebalancing despite pessimism.

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: I do think the next rally that we're going to see in markets after this uh relatively short pullback that we're looking at potentially here um will be more broad-based
claims.claim: After the pullback the next rally will be broad-based, an everything rally into year end, with a decline next year.
claims.direction: equities up broadly, then down in 2025

claims.speaker: Jim kazang
claims.quote: hang in a bit better than people might expect due to some of these Trends and I think there will be a structural weakness in Europe so I mean in the US
claims.claim: Europe and China should hold up better than expected and US weakness will be structural, so start speculating on them on a relative basis.
claims.direction: long Europe and China vs US
